patient.chief_complaint: Worsening confusion with fever and urinary symptoms
patient.history_present_illness: Ms. T. is a 55-year-old Black woman with hepatitis B cirrhosis (Child-Pugh B) and prior hepatic encephalopathy who was brought to the emergency department by her daughter for worsening confusion over the past 36 hours. The daughter arrived for her daily check and found her mother disoriented — she could not remember the current year and was confused about her location. The daughter also noted her mother had been complaining of pain with urination and lower abdominal pain for 5 days but had self-medicated with cranberry juice and refused to call her doctor. On arrival the patient has a temperature of 38.6°C, heart rate 114, and blood pressure 106/62. Right lower quadrant tenderness and right loin pain are present. Urinalysis shows 2+ bacteria, 2+ WBC, positive nitrites, and positive leukocyte esterase. The ammonia on admission is 156 µmol/L — markedly elevated. EEG shows generalized slowing with triphasic waves. CT head shows no structural abnormality. Ascites is present on exam.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Hepatic encephalopathy (West Haven grade III), hepatitis B cirrhosis (Child-Pugh B, MELD 18) — precipitated by E. coli urosepsis (UTI); ascites mandates SBP exclusion.

differential.key_features: Cultures + lactate; supportive ICU care if shock.
Check HBV DNA if not recently done; antiviral therapy continuation.
Not supported in HBV cirrhotic; tox screen.

optimal_actions.action: Comprehensive labs: CMP including AST/ALT/bilirubin/INR/albumin, ammonia, CBC, glucose, electrolytes (Na, K, Mg), BUN/Cr, lactate, blood cultures and urine cultures; toxicology if substance use plausible. Confirms liver dysfunction and screens for precipitants.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Ammonia 156; leukocytosis; urinalysis pyuria; HBV DNA if available; cultures.

optimal_actions.action: Non-contrast CT head — exclude structural alternate cause of AMS (hemorrhage, large stroke, mass) before any LP.
Literature/guideline search to confirm West Haven grading, precipitant management, and lactulose/rifaximin dosing (AASLD/EASL HE; infection-precipitated HE; HBV management).
optimal_actions.expected_finding: AASLD/EASL 2014 guidance retrieved; West Haven criteria and precipitant-driven management framework confirmed.

optimal_actions.action: Drug-interaction and medication-reconciliation review covering antibiotic selection; lactulose; rifaximin; continue HBV antiviral; flag any CNS depressants (benzodiazepines, opioids, sedating antiemetics, antihistamines) and confirm lactulose/rifaximin dosing in liver disease.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Sedating/CNS-depressant medications identified; lactulose and rifaximin reviewed for hepatic dose adjustment.

optimal_actions.action: Diagnostic paracentesis to exclude concurrent SBP.

EEG — confirm HE pattern. Triphasic waves are classic but non-specific (metabolic encephalopathies broadly); main role is exclusion of non-convulsive status epilepticus where the differential supports it.
Consult hepatology + ID — coordinate definitive care, transplant candidacy assessment where applicable.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Hepatology / critical-care guidance integrated into management.

useless_tools.rationale: No clinical suspicion for hepatopulmonary syndrome, portopulmonary hypertension, or endocarditis; echocardiography is not part of the HE workup.
Amyloid PET has no role in HE workup; reversible metabolic encephalopathy is the issue, not Alzheimer pathology.
DaTscan has no role in HE workup; the question is metabolic encephalopathy, not nigrostriatal degeneration.
Early-onset AD genetic panel has no role in HE workup; reversible metabolic encephalopathy is the diagnosis under consideration.

sequence_constraints.reason: In altered mental status, exclude intracranial mass effect / hemorrhage on imaging before LP to avoid herniation risk.

critical_actions: Empiric IV antibiotics for E. coli UTI (e.g., ceftriaxone) pending sensitivities.
Lactulose to 2-4 stools/day; rifaximin 550 mg BID.
contraindicated_actions: Do not prescribe benzodiazepines for anxiety/agitation — they precipitate and prolong HE (use haloperidol or non-pharmacologic measures for agitation).
Do not prescribe sedating opioids — they worsen HE; consider acetaminophen at hepatic-safe dosing for pain.
Do not perform LP before neuroimaging excludes mass effect when the patient has altered mental status.
Do not stop HBV antiviral therapy during acute illness (flare risk).
key_reasoning_points: HE is a clinical diagnosis: West Haven grading + evidence of liver dysfunction + exclusion of other causes of AMS — ammonia level is supportive only and correlates poorly with grade (AASLD 2014).

Precipitant identification is more actionable than the ammonia number: infection (SBP especially), GI bleed, electrolyte disturbance (hypokalemia/hyponatremia), constipation, sedative/CNS-depressant use, dehydration, dietary protein load, renal failure.
HBV cirrhotics on suppressive antivirals should not have therapy interrupted during acute illness.

metadata.difficulty_description: Straightforward HE: hepatitis B cirrhosis with urosepsis (E. coli UTI) as precipitant; hypokalemia-driven ammoniagenesis; SBP/UTI coexistence teaching point; HCC within Milan criteria for transplant
